reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises. The hypothesis makes specific claims about Cr-induced spinel formation on Q235 steel, its self-healing behavior, and its protective performance across temperature regimes, but none of these are backed by referenced prior studies.
premises: A thin Cr layer on Q235 steel can be deposited and annealed at ~850 °C to form a continuous Fe–Cr spinel oxide layer
The Fe–Cr spinel layer is self-healing and retards corrosion under both room-temperature and 700–900 °C aggressive salt conditions
The spinel layer limits oxidation, salt-induced degradation, microcracking, and spallation compared to untreated Q235 steel
The protective mechanism requires a uniform Cr layer and sufficient annealing, and may fail with rough/contaminated substrates or deviated process parameters
